adversarial_audit.objection: Many small pairwise angles can create an early intersection anyway.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Not before m reaches n/2 under the exact 1/(n-1) pairwise bound and the no-common-range premise.

adversarial_audit.objection: The theorem handles the natural portfolio directly.
adversarial_audit.resolution: No. Exact common ranges proliferate in the natural scaling records, so a common-core resolver is a prerequisite.

adversarial_audit.objection: Logarithmic certified depth covers the full k=Theta(n log n) tree.
adversarial_audit.resolution: It covers only the first O(log n) levels. The majority of the tree has linear or larger child width.

adversarial_audit.objection: Pairwise common generation of every intersection is now proved.
adversarial_audit.resolution: The theorem says emergent intersections require exact common ranges at early width; it does not prove those ranges span the full child intersection after quotienting.

claim_gate.reason: Noncommon correlations cannot create early fractional channels, but exact common ranges are prevalent and widths from Theta(n) through n! remain uncontrolled.

falsifiers_triggered: Do not search for emergent noncommon intersections at constant or sublinear child width before resolving exact common ranges.
Do not extrapolate the coherence bound beyond m<n/2.
Do not call early-level localization a full sampler without a coherent common-range decomposition and large-width theorem.

proof_obligations.resolution: Block row-sum bounds control child conditioning and the cross Gram; orthonormalization yields equation (1).
The exact pair-angle theorem supplies c<=1/(n-1) whenever the pair has no exact trivial/sign common range.
Every applicable curated W5 four-leaf control has zero child-span intersection.
Natural families have many exact common ranges; no circuit yet decomposes all of them before applying the bound.
At m=Theta(n), accumulated noncommon correlations can make the coherence bound reach one.

summary: Proved that common-free orientation families cannot develop child-span intersections while each child has fewer than n/2 leaves. This localizes early fractional channels to exact common ranges; linear-width overlap and a coherent common-range resolver remain open.

theorem_contract.cross_gram_bound: ||G_LR||<=m c by the block Schur test.
theorem_contract.pairwise_premise: Every distinct leaf pair has zero common range and principal correlation at most c.
theorem_contract.polar_consequence: At common-free early nodes the relative effect has only exact endpoint channels; no fractional intersection can emerge.
theorem_contract.scope: The theorem is conditional on removing/resolving all exact pairwise common ranges and becomes vacuous at linear child width.
theorem_contract.wreath_substitution: With c=1/(n-1), the bound is m/(n-m), strictly below one for m<n/2.
